review_mode: independent read-only source/pinned-semantics/log review; no builds or source edits
checks: Unconditional M fit is sound for independently word-bounded activeWords/offset/length: positive span can exceed one word numerically, but ceil((offset+length)/32) is still strictly below2^256; zero length returns original activeWords. Arithmetic is Nat before word conversion.

expansion removes the actual UInt256 modulus with the proved fit and derives both monotonic activeWords and positive access end≤32*actual post words. Zero-length offsets are deliberately unconstrained.
span uses actual input stack positions for CALLDATACOPY, MSTORE/MSTORE8, LOG0, RETURN and REVERT. Successful raw-step inversion excludes stack-underflow cases before using operands.
REVERT matches the pinned implementation double M application (evmReturn then evmRevert), composing monotonic bounds instead of assuming a single metadata update.
Remaining allowed operations preserve metadata; DUP/SWAP use direct primitive inversion. No recursive opcode is hidden in this allowed runtime union.
accepted uses actual runtime At→allowed proof, actual positive-fuel dispatcher and Z_ok_state; Z changes gas only, so input stack/activeWords match pre. No input cap or no-wrap premise.

runs transports actual site membership and monotonic capacity through XRuns induction. suffix_bounds uses literal actual prefix/edge/suffix with matching fuel and states, deriving intermediate and access bounds solely from final cap.
scope_limits: Image is the checked runtime site interface, instantiated for the two pinned protected runtimes; not arbitrary foreign bytecode.
Metadata bounds alone do not establish physical allocation safety, memory byte correspondence, or executable reference replay.
Positive terminal RETURN/REVERT metadata is covered by accepted; XRuns and suffix_bounds concern nonhalting edges, so final Halt must be handled separately.
Monotonicity alone does not identify each exact source memory charge; a subsequent meter consumer needs exact post-M equality and source-shaped charge differences.
